Title: Toward the Observability of Cloud-Native Applications: The Overview of the State-of-the-Art
Authors: J. Kosińska, B. Baliś, M. Konieczny, M. Malawski, S. Zieliński
Abstract: Cloud-native applications (CNAs) deployed in dynamic containerized environments require observability beyond traditional monitoring. This study provides a comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art in CNA observability, analyzing approaches, requirement types, and architectural tooling across infrastructure and microservices.

Title: A Survey on Observability of Distributed Edge & Container-Based Microservices
Authors: M. Usman, S. Ferlin, A. Brunstrom, J. Taheri
Abstract: Distributed edge and container-based microservices introduce severe challenges for performance debugging and fault localization. This survey reviews telemetry collection methods, open-source frameworks, and correlation strategies across distributed microservice topologies.

Title: Observability in Microservices: An In-Depth Exploration of Frameworks, Challenges, and Deployment Paradigms
Authors: U. Faseeha, H. Jamil Syed, F. Samad, S. Zehra, H. Ahmed
Abstract: Investigates microservice observability across emerging deployment paradigms, comparing sidecar proxies and eBPF-based kernel instrumentation for real-time performance tracking in Kubernetes.

Title: A Systematic Mapping Study on Observability of Microservices-Based Applications: Fundamentals, Classifications, and Challenges
Authors: F. Gomes, P. Rego, F. Trinta
Abstract: A systematic mapping study analyzing 66 studies on microservices observability, establishing classifications, benchmark datasets, and challenges in triggering automated autoscaling in cloud-native platforms.

Title: Holistic Root Cause Analysis for Failures in Cloud-Native Systems Through Observability Data
Authors: Y. Han, Q. Du, Y. Huang, P. Li, X. Shi, J. Wu, P. Fang, F. Tian, C. He
Abstract: Addresses inconsistent problem formulations in cloud-native failure diagnosis by proposing a holistic root cause localization model based on multimodal observability data and topology graph learning.

Title: Cloud-Native Computing: A Survey From the Perspective of Services
Authors: S. Deng, H. Zhao, B. Huang, C. Zhang, F. Chen, Y. Deng, J. Yin, S. Dustdar, A. Y. Zomaya
Abstract: Surveys cloud-native computing across service design, orchestration, and lifecycle operations, detailing architectural patterns, observability requirements, and green computing research directions.

Title: Anomaly Detection in Cloud-Native B5G Systems Using Observability and Machine Learning COTS Solutions
